action_items: Jordan Lee: Share benchmark spreadsheet + annotations (due 2026-07-23)
Priya Raman: Prepare kernel/quantization notes and recommended config for 2x latency improvement (due 2026-07-24)

summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results comparing Redwood POC run to customer baseline provider. Redwood outperforms baseline on p50 token latency and throughput for batch workloads when KV cache and batching enabled, but p95 latency with cold starts and high concurrency shows regressions tied to autoscaling/concurrency knobs. Action items set to share raw data, run 95th percentile stress tests, and schedule deep dive on quantization and cache settings.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 10:00 PT — 45 minutes. Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Rwd SE), Marcus (VeraHealth Head of Infra), Leah (VeraHealth ML), Tom (VeraHealth Security), Sofia (Product).

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — we'll run through the benchmark sheet, callout differences vs your baseline provider, then talk tuning and next steps.
[00:15] Marcus Nguyen: sounds good, yeah we pulled your spreadsheet earlier, thanks for sending it over. Quick note, some of the column headers were munged in the export so we matched on test_id.
[00:28] Priya Raman: okay great, i'll share my screen, uh lemme pull up the perf dashboard. (screen share) you should see the test run id RW-VERA-0707 and the baseline run BL-VERA-0707.
[00:43] Priya Raman: top line — p50 token latency, Redwood hosted with caching enabled shows ~12ms/token for the gpt-medium style model we primed, baseline provider shows ~18ms/token. throughput at steady state: Redwood 220 tokens/sec per GPU, baseline 150 tokens/sec.
[01:02] Leah Ortiz: those per-token numbers look promising. how are you measuring sequence length? our payloads vary 40-120 tokens, averages around 78.
[01:14] Priya Raman: good Q — we used the sequence distribution Leah sent last week, mean 78, 95th ~112. the tests included mixed sequence lengths to reflect your traffic.
[01:29] Evan Cho: one caveat is p95 — when we simulate cold sessions and autoscale events, the baseline actually edges Redwood on p95 in the 2-5s tail for a small subset of tests. that's tied to warmup latency and model variant fallbacks.
[01:47] Marcus Nguyen: hmm that matches what we saw in our in-house runs. p95 tail is our main worry, it's customer-facing. can you show the exact runs where that happens?
[02:00] Priya Raman: yeah open the run list — look at RW-VERA-0707-04 and BL-VERA-0707-03. you'll see the p95 for Redwood ~1.2s for the heavy concurrent test vs baseline ~900ms on that particular config.
[02:20] Jordan Lee: to be clear, overall Redwood gives better steady-state throughput and lower median latency, but the cold-start/scale-out points need tuning — we think this is autoscaler threshold and pre-warming behavior.
[02:35] Tom Baker: are there any differences in how you manage KV cache across replicas? we saw cache misses possibly causing higher tail.
[02:45] Priya Raman: yes, by default the KV cache is local to the inference worker; we do cross-request prefix caching where possible but on scale events new workers will have cold KV caches. recommended config is to enable small warmup slices and keep a hot pool of standby replicas for spikes.
[03:03] Marcus Nguyen: can you quantify the cost delta if we increase the hot pool? our finance team will want numbers.
[03:12] Evan Cho: roughly, keeping a 2-replica hot pool increases cost by ~18% but drops p95 tail by ~40% in our sim. we'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:28] Leah Ortiz: what about quantization? we are open to 4-bit if accuracy holds. did you run any quantized model variants?
[03:36] Priya Raman: yes we ran INT8 and Q4_0. Q4_0 showed ~1.3x improvement in tokens/sec and small median latency gains; end-to-end accuracy on your eval set dropped 0.7% F1 on intent extraction, within your tolerance bracket per last week's convo, but we need to confirm across more eval prompts.
[03:58] Sofia Reyes: small drop maybe OK, but we need to be sure on edge cases. can you attach the eval prompt set?
[04:06] Jordan Lee: yes we'll include the eval set link and the diff report.
[04:12] [05:00] Speaker 1: (mumble) — sorry, little bit of background noise, i missed the last point about fallback models.
[05:10] Priya Raman: fallback — Redwood can route to a smaller quantized model variant when latency targets are missed or when cost tiering is needed. for instance, route to RWD-compact-q4 during spikes and fall back to your primary model after.
[05:27] Marcus Nguyen: can that be region-aware? our EU traffic must stay in eu-west and we have residency constraints.
[05:35] Evan Cho: yes routing policies include region pins, model variant compatibility check, and automatic fallback as an ordered list. we'll show config snippets.
[05:50] Tom Baker: security question — if you use a hot pool of standby replicas, are they part of the same VPC and under our KMS? we need to ensure keys aren't shared outside our tenant.
[06:02] Priya Raman: for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and VPC isolation, hot pool replicas would be inside the same account and KMS scope. for hosted we'll provide encryption in transit at rest but not customer KMS unless in dedicated/private mode.
[06:20] Tom Baker: ok that's helpful, we'll follow up with exact KMS requirements.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: back to numbers — i'll call out a few rows: RW run 07 shows steady-state throughput at 220 tok/s and median 12ms/token. BL run 03 shows 150 tok/s and 18ms/token. p95 for RW in mixed-concurrency test is 1.2s; BL is 900ms for that test.
[06:52] Leah Ortiz: do you have histograms? percentiles between p50 and p95?
[06:58] Priya Raman: yes histogram links are in sheet column H — but rough shape shows bimodal tail during scale events.
[07:10] Marcus Nguyen: what about batching settings? our devs worry about latency variability with bigger batch sizes.
[07:20] Evan Cho: we tested auto-batching up to 32 tokens per batch; for low-latency routes we recommend max_batch_size 8 and dynamic batching window 10ms. that gives most of the throughput benefit without big p95 regression.
[07:36] Leah Ortiz: and caching prefixes — how big? our typical prompt context is around 1k tokens of system + history.
[07:45] Priya Raman: we keep kv-cache size tuned to your typical active context, default 2048 entries is overkill; we recommended 1024 for your workload which reduces cache misses and memory. we'll attach config.
[07:58] Sofia Reyes: can you repeat the cost comparison with quantized + hot pool vs baseline?
[08:06] Evan Cho: quick off the cuff: baseline monthly estimate (based on your traffic) ~ $12k/mo; Redwood with quantized models and a 2-replica hot pool ~ $9.6k/mo (20% savings). raw numbers will be in sheet.
[08:22] Marcus Nguyen: good. we need that broken down per route and per 95th-percentile scenario for finance.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll break down by route and include p50/p95 columns.
[08:36] [10:00] Speaker 2: (inaudible) — did you guys evaluate spot instance interruptions?
[10:10] Priya Raman: our POC runs used on-demand GPUs for stability; we can run a spot simulation but that changes tail characteristics. if you plan to use spot we'll include interruption-resilient configs and checkpoint warmups.
[10:30] Leah Ortiz: one more — inference runtimes: are you running your own optimized kernels or relying on the vendor framework?
[10:38] Priya Raman: Redwood runtime picks kernels at runtime — a mix of vendor BLAS and Redwood-optimized fused kernels. we profiled kernel hotpaths for your model and saw a 15% improvement vs vanilla vendor stack. we'll include flamegraphs.
[10:55] Marcus Nguyen: do you support our internal apm hooks? we need traces sent to our datadog instance.
[11:02] Evan Cho: yes we have tracing hooks and export options; can push spans to datadog or open telemetry collector. we'll share the integration doc.
[11:16] Tom Baker: regarding compliance — audit logs, retention etc — are those in the POC?
[11:24] Priya Raman: audit logs were enabled for the runs and retained for 90 days in the POC. for enterprise we can configure retention and S3 integration or SIEM exports.
[11:36] Jordan Lee: ok, to surface recommended tuning steps: 1) increase hot pool to 2 replicas for spike protection; 2) enable Q4 quantization for non-critical routes; 3) set max_batch_size 8 and dynamic window 10ms; 4) smaller KV cache tuned to 1024 entries. point 2 and 3 expected to give net median and throughput gains, point 1 will improve p95 at cost bump.
[12:05] Leah Ortiz: sounds actionable. how do we validate accuracy drift from quantization?
[12:12] Priya Raman: we'll run your eval harness across 5k prompts and provide per-prompt diffs and an aggregated metric with failure cases highlighted.
[12:25] Marcus Nguyen: timeline — can you get the raw spreadsheet and configs by tomorrow?
[12:31] Jordan Lee: yes, action item for me to share everything by EOD tomorrow.
[12:36] Sofia Reyes: and let's set the deep dive next Friday to go through kernel-level profiling, quantization caveats, and security checklist.
[12:43] Jordan Lee: noted, i'll send calendar invite.
[12:47] [15:00] Speaker 3: quick nit — some of the labels in the sheet refer to 'openai' oddly, is that a baseline tag?
[15:10] Priya Raman: apology, some early test tags were templated; BL refers to your internal baseline provider, not openai in this case. we'll clean that up.
[15:24] Tom Baker: last question — network egress patterns when using private deployment? we need to ensure no leaks to public endpoints.
[15:32] Evan Cho: private deployment keeps all inference traffic inside the VPC, control plane calls can be routed through our control plane or be self-hosted; we'll provide a network diagram.
[15:45] Marcus Nguyen: perfect.
[15:50] Jordan Lee: ok wrap up — we'll share the sheet, perf graphs, eval diffs, and config snippets. next steps: VeraHealth to run 95th percentile stress test with 100 concurrent users and share results, Redwood to prepare quantization notes and cost breakdown.
[16:08] Leah Ortiz: thanks all. one more thing, can you include the exact docker image tags used in the run?
[16:14] Priya Raman: yes docker tags + commit sha in sheet.
[16:20] Jordan Lee: great, thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches (speaker splits and mislabels). Shared artifacts: https://redwood-internal.app/perf/runs/RW-VERA-0707, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/VERA-benchmark (redwood to share full access).
